level.title: A1 Beginner Tamil
goals: Understand and produce level-appropriate Tamil in real contexts.
Read target script with consistent romanisation support.
Use respectful, age-friendly language with cultural awareness.

lessons.title: Greetings and Respect
lessons.learn: Learn greetings used across Tamil-speaking communities. Tamil is read left to right. Use நீங்கள் (nīṅkaḷ) with elders and new people; spoken forms may differ from formal written forms.

grammar.title: Respectful identity sentences
grammar.explain: Tamil commonly omits an overt “is” in simple identity sentences. Pronouns and respectful forms carry social meaning.

examples.t: வணக்கம்! நான் கார்த்திக். நீங்கள் எப்படி இருக்கிறீர்கள்?
examples.r: Vaṇakkam! Nāṉ Kārttik. Nīṅkaḷ eppaḍi irukkiṟīrkaḷ?
examples.en: Hello! I'm Karthik. How are you?

examples.t: நான் நன்றாக இருக்கிறேன், நன்றி. நீங்கள் எந்த ஊர்?
examples.r: Nāṉ naṉṟāka irukkiṟēṉ, naṉṟi. Nīṅkaḷ enta ūr?
examples.en: I'm fine, thank you. Which town are you from?

mistakes: Do not use informal நீ (nī) automatically with an elder or stranger.

lessons.title: People and Pronouns
lessons.learn: Identify people and choose singular, plural, and respectful pronouns. Learn complete forms with romanisation before analysing suffixes.

grammar.title: Pronouns and zero copula
grammar.explain: A present identity statement often places the description after the person without a separate word for “is.”

lessons.title: குடும்பமும் உறவுகளும்
lessons.learn: Name the people in a family and say who someone is to you. என் introduces one person's relation; எங்கள் introduces the family as a group. In Tamil, the familiar kin term can also be a warm form of address, but this lesson keeps the respectful நீங்கள் for a new adult.

grammar.title: My family
grammar.pattern: என் + kin term · அவர் என் ... · எங்கள் குடும்பம்
grammar.explain: Possession comes before the noun: என் அண்ணன். For a person's role, say அவர் என் அப்பா. The pronoun அவர் is respectful and takes the plural-like அவர் இருக்கிறார் form, even when referring to one person.

examples.en: There are four people in our family.

mistakes.why: The simple introduction places இவர் first.
Respectful அவர் takes இருக்கிறார், not the familiar இருக்கிறான்.

dialogue.en: Who is this?
This is my mother.
How many people are there in your family?

dialogue.t: நான்கு பேர். என் அப்பா, அம்மா, தங்கை, நான்.
dialogue.r: nāṉku pēr. eṉ appā, ammā, taṅkai, nāṉ.
dialogue.en: Four people: my father, mother, younger sister, and me.

lessons.title: Home, School, and Objects
lessons.learn: Name familiar places and objects, then locate them. Tamil attaches case endings to nouns rather than placing separate prepositions before them.

grammar.title: Location with -இல் / -ல
grammar.explain: The formal locative suffix -இல் (-il), often -ல (-la) in speech, means “in/at.”
mistakes: Do not put a Tamil location marker before the noun as English does.

lessons.title: கடையில் வாங்குதல்
lessons.learn: Ask a shopkeeper for a quantity and the price. ஒரு கிலோ, அரை கிலோ and இரண்டு பழம் name amounts; வேண்டும் states what you need, while எவ்வளவு? asks the price. Put the item and quantity before the verb வேண்டும்.

grammar.title: Amounts and requests
grammar.explain: வேண்டும் follows the thing requested: இரண்டு கிலோ தக்காளி வேண்டும். To ask about a price, use எவ்வளவு?; the answer is a number followed by ரூபாய். The measure word follows the number.

examples.en: I need one kilogram of tomatoes.
Half a kilo is twenty rupees.

mistakes.why: Keep the quantity next to the item, before வேண்டும்.

dialogue.en: Hello. I need one kilogram of tomatoes.

dialogue.r: arai kilō veṅkāyamum vēṇṭum. vilai evvaḷavu?
dialogue.en: I also need half a kilo of onions. What is the price?
Sixty rupees in total.

lessons.title: பேருந்து நிலையத்தில்
lessons.learn: Ask which bus goes to a place and understand a simple direction. The destination takes -க்கு; எங்கே? asks where, and நேராக / வலப்பக்கம் / இடப்பக்கம் give a short route. In a respectful request, say சொல்லுங்கள் rather than சொல்.

grammar.title: Destinations and directions
grammar.explain: The destination marker -க்கு joins to the place: மதுரைக்கு. Ask எப்படிப் போவது? (how to go?) and listen for a sequence: முதலில் (first), பிறகு (then). The respectful instruction ends with -ுங்கள்.

The bus station is quite nearby.

mistakes.why: Use the respectful imperative with a new person.

Five minutes. The station is at the end of the road.

culture.text: Tamil is one of the longest continuously written languages in the world, and its script is an abugida: every consonant carries an inherent அ unless a vowel sign changes it, and a pulli (்) removes the vowel altogether. The script the course teaches is the written register — செந்தமிழ், 'correct Tamil' — while everyday speech shortens the same words (வருகிறேன் → வர்றேன்). Both are Tamil, and the course says which one it is teaching at every step; Thirukkural couplets and film songs are quoted from memory in the same households that speak the shortened forms.

reading.text: தமிழ் என் தாய்மொழி. நான் சென்னையில் பிறந்தேன், இப்போது பெங்களூரில் வேலை செய்கிறேன். வீட்டில் தமிழ் பேசுகிறோம், கடையில் ஆங்கிலம். வாரம் ஒருமுறை அம்மாவுக்குத் தொலைபேசி செய்கிறேன். என் மகள் இப்போது தமிழ் எழுதப் பழகுகிறாள்; முதலில் உயிர் எழுத்துகள், பிறகு மெய் எழுத்துகள். அவளுக்குப் பிடித்த எழுத்து ழ.
reading.gloss: Tamil is my mother tongue. I was born in Chennai and now work in Bengaluru. At home we speak Tamil, at the shop English. Once a week I telephone my mother. My daughter is now learning to write Tamil; first the vowels, then the consonants. Her favourite letter is ழ.

listening.script: வணக்கம், நான் ரவி. நீங்கள் எந்த ஊர்? — நான் மதுரை. தமிழ் கற்றுக்கொண்டிருக்கிறேன். — நல்லது, மெதுவாகப் பேசுகிறேன்.
listening.gloss: Hello, I am Ravi. Which town are you from? — I am from Madurai. I am learning Tamil. — Good, I will speak slowly.

mistakes.why: A name takes the genitive என், not the dative எனக்கு.
Tamil is head-final: the verb comes last.
The respectful நீங்கள் takes the plural imperative.

task.title: என்னை அறிமுகம் செய்யுங்கள்
task.instructions: Write six sentences introducing yourself in Tamil: your name, your town, your work or study, one language you speak, what you do at home, and one thing you are learning. Use நான் with the -கிறேன் present, and the respectful நீங்கள் once in a question. Read it aloud twice: once slowly for the letters, once at speaking speed. Then write the same six sentences with a different subject (அவர், அவள், அவர்கள்) and check that the verb ending changes.

pronunciation.t: Tamil contrasts short and long vowels.
pronunciation.tip: Hold long vowels about twice as long; length can change meaning.

pronunciation.t: ழ is a distinct Tamil sound.
pronunciation.tip: Curl the tongue back gently and let the sound flow along the sides.

pronunciation.t: ள and ல are different lateral sounds.
pronunciation.tip: Use a curled tongue for ள and a forward tongue for ல.

pronunciation.t: ண and ந distinguish tongue position.
pronunciation.tip: Curl back for ண; place the tongue forward for ந.
Listen to whole words; many stops become voiced between vowels.

alphabet.title: Tamil Script Foundations
alphabet.explain: Only 31 letters — no aspirates, no separate voiced sounds. க reads ka, ga or kha depending on position: one letter, three jobs. Fewer letters to learn, more listening to do. Spoken Tamil also shortens many written forms — this course teaches the written form first and flags the street version.

counting.title: Tamil Numbers
counting.explain: Tamil counts directly — people take the word பேர் (persons):
rules: Place a number before its noun in a basic counted phrase.
Learn one to twenty as whole forms before building larger quantities.
